extraction.rai:dataCollection: Small toy datasets were created by using annotations from the validation split of the COCO dataset to determine image content, such as the presence of a person or the type of sport being played, and then generating specific questions based on those annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Annotations and images from the validation split of the COCO dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for images by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers generated the answers. For Visual Genome, annotators asked free-form questions or were prompted to ask questions about specific image regions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Multiple answers per question were collected to compute consensus-based evaluation metrics, including average consensus, min consensus, and an accuracy metric where a full score is awarded if an algorithm agrees with three or more annotators.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Language biases in questions; consistent context and biases in natural image datasets; bias toward 'yes' answers in binary questions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small for complex models, contains exclusively indoor scenes, and has cluttered/poorly lit images; COCO-QA contains awkwardly phrased, grammatically incorrect, or unintelligible questions; COCO-VQA contains subjective, opinion-seeking questions lacking objective answers and suffers from annotator unreliability; dataset biases impair the ability to properly evaluate VQA algorithms.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA can act as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images on the web and in the real world.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Aid to blind and visually impaired individuals; improving human-computer interaction to query visual content; image retrieval without meta-data or tags; basic research and visual Turing tests for image understanding.
